clue.text: A child of four

parts.note: reads as a youngster aged four, but means one of four babies born at a single birth

explanation.surface: Someone mentions a youngster who is four years old.
explanation.definitionFit: One of four siblings delivered together at one birth is so called, a literal child among four.

clue.text: Important-sounding landing-place

indicators.note: sounding tells us the word for important is heard, then written another way

parts.note: key means crucial or important

explanation.surface: An important-seeming spot to come ashore.
explanation.definitionFit: A wharf or harbour platform is where boats land cargo and passengers.

clue.text: Having the power to remove the top of the board

indicators.note: remove the top of means the opening letter of the word for board is dropped

parts.note: a table is a board, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: Someone has authority to strip the leading member off a committee.
explanation.definitionFit: Being capable means having the means or skill to do something.

clue.text: Other gear, say, be included for music

indicators.note: be included means the abbreviation for say goes inside the rearranged letters
other suggests a different version, so the letters of gear are reordered

parts.note: EG, for example, is what say means

explanation.surface: Different equipment is brought in for a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Other' makes RGAE from GEAR, and 'be included' puts EG inside it after R.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jamaican popular style with offbeat rhythms is a genre of music.

clue.text: Costly end of hostilities

parts.note: a truce bought dearly: ending a war whatever sacrifice it demands

explanation.surface: A war ends at great cost.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes seeking a ceasefire regardless of the cost, so an expensive armistice is a playful literal reading.

clue.text: Of a very early period once perhaps in Early English

indicators.note: in puts the rearranged letters between the two abbreviation letters

parts.note: EE is the abbreviation for Early English, the architectural style

indicators.note: perhaps hints that once is only one possible order of its letters

explanation.surface: Something from long ago, possibly in Early English architecture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' turns ONCE into OCEN, and 'in' puts it between the two Es.
explanation.definitionFit: This geological epoch, about 56 to 34 million years ago, belongs to remote prehistory.

clue.text: Copied in a beastly way

parts.note: beastly suggests nastily, but it means in the way of a beast, as monkeys mimic humans

explanation.surface: Someone imitated another person rather nastily.
explanation.definitionFit: To mimic is to do as primates do, so imitating like a beast is a fair cryptic description.

clue.text: Appropriate fact

definitions.meaning: specific or belonging to one case, suitable to it
a detail or item of information

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means specific or fitting; as a noun a single detail or point of information.

clue.text: Diana has requested that it be put in a confusing way!

parts.note: Di is the short form of the name Diana
the 's in contractions like she's can stand for has
ordered means asked for, as in a restaurant

explanation.surface: Diana asks for something to be arranged in a muddled way.
explanation.definitionFit: Something jumbled or muddled is arranged without order.

clue.text: Loyalty, say, in kinship

indicators.note: the abbreviation for say is placed in the word for kinship

parts.note: an alliance is a bond or relationship between parties
EG, for example, is what say means

explanation.surface: Loyalty is said to come from family ties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts EG inside ALLIANCE, splitting it after ALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean faithfulness or devotion owed to a cause or ruler.

clue.text: Lover wounded back

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for wounded from right to left

parts.note: sore means hurt or wounded

explanation.surface: A lover has been injured in the back.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek god of love is a byword for a lover or desire.

clue.text: One in court to deal with trespassers?

definitions.text: One in court to deal with trespassers?

parts.words: One in court to deal with trespassers?
parts.note: trespassers suggests people on private land, but also means sinners or wrongdoers whom a legal officer pursues in a courtroom

explanation.surface: A landowner sends someone to court over intruders.
explanation.definitionFit: The lawyer who presents the case against an accused offender in a trial.

clue.text: Irregular part of the main Constantinople area

indicators.note: part of says the letters lie within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A changeable district of Constantinople by the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts with the last two letters of 'main'; 'area' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fickle or variable is not steady or regular.

clue.text: Attendant has a book on the spectacle

parts.note: a page is a young attendant or servant
NT, the New Testament, is a book of the Bible

explanation.surface: A servant carries a book into a grand show.
explanation.definitionFit: A colourful public procession or show is a spectacle.

clue.text: Fruit that was satisfying will go down quickly

parts.note: a plum is a fruit
met, as in met the needs, means satisfied

explanation.surface: A fruit that once filled us will drop quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop steeply or fall headlong, as prices or a falling body do.

clue.text: A popular little paper

parts.note: little suggests a scrap but refers to a newspaper of smaller page size aimed at a mass readership

explanation.surface: Someone describes a well-liked small sheet of paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A small-format newspaper with a mass readership and sensational stories.

clue.text: Right joint to become inflamed

parts.note: the ankle is a joint of the leg

explanation.surface: A right ankle swells up painfully.
explanation.definitionFit: In its older sense a wound that festers or grows sore is said to do this, as does a grievance.

clue.text: It is less trouble to see air moving!

indicators.note: moving means the letters of the words see air shift into a new order

explanation.surface: It is simpler to watch the breeze.
explanation.definitionFit: Something less troublesome is simpler or more straightforward.

clue.text: Thunderous clapping?

parts.note: suggests thunderclaps in bad weather but means loud, sustained applause from an audience

explanation.surface: Thunder claps in a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: A tumultuous ovation is described with weather imagery: a sudden outburst of cheering and hands beating together.

clue.text: Money we exchanged for fruit

parts.note: cash is money

indicators.note: exchanged signals the two letters of we swap places

explanation.surface: Someone trades money for some fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The kidney-shaped nut grows on a tropical tree whose swollen stalk is the cashew apple, so it counts as a fruit.

clue.text: The man, after the court order, to squirm

indicators.note: after means the word for the man is placed behind the writ

parts.note: a writ is a written order issued by a court
he refers to a man

explanation.surface: A man served with a court order wriggles uncomfortably.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean to twist and turn the body in discomfort.

clue.text: Fodder plant I left inside

indicators.note: inside places I and the abbreviation for left within the herb

parts.note: sage is an aromatic herb, a plant

explanation.surface: A farm plant has been left to feed livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: Grass fermented and stored in a silo is winter feed for cattle.

clue.text: Small group once let it stand outside

indicators.note: outside means the proofreader's mark goes around the word for once

parts.note: stet is the Latin proofreading mark meaning let it stand
ex means former, as in ex-wife

explanation.surface: A small group once agreed to leave things as they were.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' places STET around EX, splitting it after S.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of six musicians or singers is a small ensemble.

clue.text: Go back quietly inside when caught

indicators.note: inside means the soft letter is placed within the reversed word
back means the word for go is read from right to left

parts.note: to depart is to go or leave
P, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Someone sneaks back silently when they get caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns DEPART into TRAPED, and 'inside' puts P within it after TRAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Being snared or captured is to be caught.

clue.text: Old vehicle, a steamer stopping short

indicators.note: stopping short means the last letter of the word for the steamer is cut off

parts.note: a tramp steamer is a cargo ship with no fixed route

explanation.surface: An old vehicle, a steamboat, halts before reaching port.
explanation.walkthrough: A tramp is a merchant steamer that goes wherever cargo takes it; dropping its last letter leaves the vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Street trams ran in British cities before buses, and the clue treats them as a vintage form of transport.

clue.text: Little skipper?

parts.note: skipper suggests a captain, but means a young creature that jumps playfully in spring fields

explanation.surface: A small captain is at the helm.
explanation.definitionFit: A young sheep gambols and leaps about in springtime fields.

clue.text: Among the best an Olympian cup-bearer

indicators.note: among says the letters sit within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Among the finest is a servant of the gods.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the goddess of youth served nectar to the gods on Olympus.

clue.text: Fabricated tapestries can be revealing

definitions.note: the definition describes the act rather than naming it: a performance that shows off the body

indicators.note: fabricated means made up, so the letters of tapestries are built into something new

explanation.surface: Woven wall-hangings can show more than expected.
explanation.definitionFit: The cabaret act consists of slowly removing clothes, which exposes the performer.

clue.text: Rodent found by a tree in New Zealand

parts.note: a rat is a rodent

explanation.surface: A rat is discovered next to a New Zealand tree.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a Maori name for a crimson-flowered native hardwood of New Zealand.

clue.text: Belle acted in a way that was delightful

indicators.note: in a way signals that the letters of Belle acted are arranged differently

explanation.surface: Belle gave a charming performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe something pleasing, especially tasty food.
